#+title: Working with immutable build products

* Edit, build, inspect
Use ordinary commands while the environment selects the SDK, pinned tools and
build station. Application edits reuse native products; Rust or toolchain edits
select new native inputs. Keep the compiler VM warm for analysis.

#+begin_src sh
./bin/bl build
./bin/bl artifacts list
./bin/bl artifacts compare /absolute/old-receipt.json /absolute/new-receipt.json
./bin/bl artifacts explain /absolute/old-receipt.json /absolute/new-receipt.json
./bin/bl self-build --out /absolute/bin/bl
#+end_src

Build, native preparation and SDK-family production submit fixed immutable
operations through the packaged preparation coordinator. Nix shares identical
realization work. Each request retains its own inputs, result and receipt;
publication verifies the product and holds the destination's writer claim.

compare reports recorded identity differences. explain separates application
content/interface/closure/requirement changes, namespace additions/removals and
recorded reverse-dependency witnesses. Missing graph coverage stays explicit.
An unchanged interface is evidence for choosing checks, not a compatibility
certificate. See [[file:artifact-impact.org][impact explanations]].

* Feedback while developing the language
Project Source edits reuse the selected SDK and warm compiler VM. Ordinary
application production and native preparation have their own captured inputs
and Nix caches.

Editing engine inputs under priv/, bin/, nix/ or the declared bootstrap inputs
prepares a new immutable compiler/coordinator/SDK before the next cold checkout
entry. Current full engine preparation can take tens of minutes. Batch engine
edits and use bounded component checks for implementation feedback, then run
acceptance against the actual produced SDK. Component results retain their
narrow scope and do not qualify the final SDK or the original semantic cases.
The recorded plan lists the exact remaining acceptance gates.

* Configure the build station once
The managed host module routes ordinary build and self-build requests through
Nix's configured builder. A project needs no remote-build flags:

#+begin_src nix
services.beam-lisp-artifacts = {
  enable = true;
  buildStation = {
    hostName = "build-station";
    sshUser = "nix-ssh";
    sshKey = "/var/lib/nix/keys/build-station";
  };
};
#+end_src

Deploy the module through the host's configuration workflow and manage the SSH
host key there. Key bytes stay outside the Nix store. With a buildStation the
module disables local realization, configures ssh-ng and enables substitutes.
Each station requires accepted sandbox/KVM/cgroup policy and actual resource
qualification. A client process limit does not cap daemon workers. See
[[file:immutable-artifacts.bl.org][immutable artifact operation]] for host policy and receiver checks.

* Declare the inputs
Source roots and supporting files belong in env.bl:

#+begin_src clojure
{:paths ["src"]
 :build {:paths ["src"] :inputs ["schemas" "assets"] :out "build" :jobs 2
         :native [{:source "native-workspace" :member "crates/engine"
                   :package "rust-engine" :crate "engine"
                   :abi "beam-lisp-native-engine-v1"}]}}
#+end_src

The native :source is the whole Cargo workspace closure. :member selects its
package directory, :package is Cargo's package name, and :crate is the BL-facing
library alias. Root Cargo.lock, sibling path dependencies and supporting inputs
stay inside the captured root. Standalone path/glob entries and the native/*
convention remain supported. Cargo performs locked compilation inside the pinned
Nix worker; Nix supplies immutable inputs, toolchains, products and reuse.

For explicit preparation:

#+begin_src sh
./bin/bl artifacts prepare /absolute/standalone engine beam-lisp-native-engine-v1
./bin/bl artifacts prepare-workspace /absolute/workspace crates/engine rust-engine engine beam-lisp-native-engine-v1
#+end_src

Snapshots preserve bytes, executable bits, empty directories and declared
support files. Selected symlinks and inputs outside the source root refuse.
See [[file:native-workspaces.org][native workspace boundaries]].

* Failure and forced production
A failed preparation keeps the selected generation intact. Inspect its bounded
log and exact request before changing inputs. From an application project,
request a fresh application compiler execution on the configured station:

#+begin_src sh
./bin/bl build --force
#+end_src

The request and receipt retain the attempt identity. Nix's separate --rebuild
operation has different execution constraints. An engine-checkout build
projects its already selected SDK; --force does not manufacture a new SDK
identity. Engine input edits drive immutable SDK preparation on the next cold
entry.

For partial programmatic source ownership:

#+begin_src clojure
(build/run {:root project-root :out build-directory
            :sources [(str project-root "/src/example/leaf.bl")]
            :scope :scoped :jobs 2})
#+end_src

Scoped production verifies the immutable parent and retains unrelated units.
An empty scope preserves that generation; a full inventory prunes removed
sources. A changed SDK and contextual World product require full ownership.
Filesystem selection through .nix-product/units or .nix-sdk/image/lib identifies
products; runtime activation follows the existing verified-unit protocol.

* Shared requests and reconnecting
Independent callers can share Nix work without sharing writable Cargo targets
or request directories. Save a request's preparation handle to reconnect with
status!, events! or await! from another caller. An await timeout or disconnect
leaves the durable job running. Cancellation and recovery validate that request's
actual worker identity; ambiguous identity produces no signal. See
[[file:preparation-jobs.org][preparation job operations]].

* Capture and replay selected tests
Use the matching immutable SDK's direct launcher in a clean SDK context. Select
actual immutable product/source/test-source addresses and explicit fixtures in
OPTIONS_JSON, then use:

#+begin_src sh
/absolute/selected-sdk/bin/bl artifacts replay-capture /absolute/options.json /absolute/capsule.json
/absolute/selected-sdk/bin/bl artifacts replay-plan /absolute/capsule.json
/absolute/selected-sdk/bin/bl artifacts replay /absolute/capsule.json /absolute/result.json
#+end_src

Capture records actual SDK/compiler/build/native/tool identities and retains
their closures with the selected files. Plan rechecks inputs and observations.
Replay calls the ordinary isolated selected-file test path and publishes actual
counters plus digest-bound selected-test receipts to RESULT_JSON. Read that file
for machine results; test stdout can remain on the terminal. Output files are
private, exclusive and published under the existing writer claim.

Live replay accepts explicit .bl files. It requires a physically verified SDK,
current compiler/native floor and clean global context. Mutable search roots,
preloaded project definitions and project realms refuse. The resolver pins
immutable test-source as its fixed Source root. The product is retained and
checked; activation or proof that the tests consumed its compiled code requires
separate runtime integration. See [[file:artifact-replay-runner.org][replay options, receipts and receiver restrictions]].

* Update and rollback
Retain the working product while preparing a candidate. Compare its receipt,
run the intended consumer checks, and use a compatible fresh VM or the existing
runtime activation protocol. A retained prior product makes its bytes available
for rollback; native-library lifetime, running generation retirement, serving
readiness and application-data restore remain explicit runtime/deployment work.

* Capability roster
| Implemented surface | Operation | Qualification boundary |
| build / self-build | Immutable application and SDK/release production with transparent coordinator/builder routing | Current SDK, lifecycle, target and receiver checks govern promotion |
| Workspace native declarations / prepare-workspace | Explicit locked member/package selection and stable BL alias | Supported Linux x86_64 cdylib recipe; dependencies stay inside captured closure |
| artifact-jobs | Durable native/application/SDK jobs, observation, reconnect, cancellation and recovery | Product verification and writer custody precede publication |
| artifacts list / compare / explain | Retained receipts, identity differences and bounded recorded impact witnesses | Compatibility and complete rebuild scope require consumer evidence |
| artifacts capsule | Retained reproduction descriptor | Identity recording, separate test qualification |
| replay-capture / replay-plan / replay | Immutable selected inputs, actual observations, clean-context execution and receipts | Selected .bl tests only; fixed test-source root; product remains unactivated |
| Nix roots and private custody records | Explicit retention of inputs/results/tools | Retention persists until released; automatic live-consumer GC is separate work |
| Managed artifact host module | Builder routing, strict sandbox and aggregate worker limits | Deployment and actual station containment must be qualified |

* Semantic and deployment tracks
| Track | Required evidence or integration | Result |
| Current SDK/lifecycle acceptance | Real target SDK, command lifetime, cancellation/recovery and receiver controls | Promotion evidence for the selected implementation |
| Candidate comparison realms | Verified product activation, resolver ownership and realm retirement | Side-by-side checks against a candidate's compiled code |
| Broader qualification | Consumer/platform suites with real receipts | Compatibility evidence beyond selected tests |
| Mutable-state reproduction | Domain snapshot/restore and explicit secret handling | Reproduction of failures depending on external state |
| Consumer-aware retention | Real live-consumer inventory and release policy | Safe automatic root collection |

Compiler semantics, hygienic expansion, descriptor truth, execution admission
and actor/callback lifetimes remain language/runtime responsibilities. Nix
provides filesystem products; Foundry coordinates their preparation and deployment.
